problem: Existing LLM-based VLN agents only do high-level planning: they pick nodes on a predefined navigation graph. Zero-shot continuous-VLN methods (e.g. A2Nav) still need large amounts of simulator data to train low-level policies or waypoint predictors, and learned waypoint predictors (DC-VLN/ETPNav) depend on MP3D nav-graph supervision.
motivation: Practical VLN in continuous environments requires low-level motion (waypoints and obstacle-avoiding paths), not just choosing a view. LLMs are good in 2D RGB space but poor at predicting 3D coordinates directly. The observation driving the paper is that foundation models (Grounded SAM + multimodal LLMs) can find navigable ground and plan paths over it in pixel space, and that depth plus camera intrinsics can then lift those pixel paths to 3D, so no simulator training is needed.
key_idea: Segment visible ground with Grounded SAM, scatter numbered points on it (Visual Affordances Prompting), and let one multimodal LLM choose waypoints and connect points into obstacle-avoiding pixel paths. A second LLM (PathAgent) picks one path from the paths drawn on the 4 views, and the chosen pixel path is lifted to 3D with depth and intrinsics, then executed as rotate-then-forward actions.
insight: Navigational affordances are the key ingredient. On the 100-episode R2R-CE ablation subset, scattering points without SAM ground segmentation drops SR 27→15 and SPL 16.9→7.2, because many points land on obstacles and there are too many options. Including the instruction in the low-level prompt (+3 SR) and explicit waypoint definitions (obstacle clearance, crucial regions; +4 SR versus MP3D-style 2–3 m waypoints) also help, and drawing candidate paths into the images (PathAgent) beats a MapGPT-style view-selection agent by 6–7 SR. The zero-shot LLM waypoint predictor almost matches the supervised MP3D-trained predictor from DC-VLN (16.9 vs 17.6 SPL); LLMs have asymmetric strengths, with Gemini-1.5-Pro better at low-level planning and GPT-4o better at high-level decisions (the swapped pairing gets only 11 SR). Of 100 manually checked failures, ~70% come from high-level decisions and ~30% from low-level planning.
method: Navigational affordances: Grounded SAM (Grounding DINO with text prompt 'ground' + SAM) segments visible ground in each of 4 non-overlapping 90°-FOV views (front/left/back/right); the per-view masks are fused into one affordance map A_t^i.

Visual Affordances Prompting (VAP): points are distributed uniformly inside the affordance mask and drawn with numeric IDs (Set-of-Mark style). Gemini-1.5-Pro receives the low-level task description D_L (waypoint/path definitions: keep away from obstacles, land in crucial regions, connect points to route around obstacles), the instruction I and the marked view. It outputs candidate waypoint IDs W_t^i and paths P_t^i as point sequences; results from the 4 views are merged.

High-level PathAgent: all candidate paths are rendered with IDs onto the 4 observation images (O_t'). GPT-4o, with prompts adapted from MapGPT (task description D_H, instruction, history H_t), outputs a thought T_t and selects one path as action a_t.

3D mapping and motion control: each pixel point of the chosen path (a polyline) is back-projected to world coordinates using simulator depth and camera intrinsics. Each segment is executed with ETPNav's rotate-then-forward controller as ROTATE 15° / FORWARD 0.25 m actions.

Waypoint distillation (supervised variant): the LLM VAP predictor pseudo-labels ~10K locations / 40K images (40K Gemini calls, ~84 USD) to train ETPNav's waypoint predictor without MP3D nav-graph ground truth (Chamfer 1.08 vs 1.04 for the original). This predictor is combined with ETPNav's VLN agent trained on R2R-CE/RxR-CE.

setting.backbone: Gemini-1.5-Pro (frozen, low-level VAP planner) + GPT-4o (frozen, high-level PathAgent) + Grounded SAM (Grounding DINO + SAM, frozen); the distilled variant uses ETPNav's waypoint predictor + VLN agent (trained)
setting.training_data: Zero-shot variant: none (training-free). Distilled variant: ETPNav waypoint predictor trained on ~10K locations / 40K images pseudo-labeled by Gemini (no MP3D nav-graph ground truth), and ETPNav VLN agent trained on R2R-CE / RxR-CE training data (15K iterations R2R-CE, 30K iterations RxR-CE).
setting.observation: 4 non-overlapping egocentric RGB-D views (front/left/back/right, 90° FOV) + camera intrinsics; instruction and history text
setting.action_space: LLM selects a pixel path among marked affordance points → lifted to 3D waypoints → low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / ROTATE 15° / STOP via a rotate-then-forward controller
setting.privileged: none (uses simulator depth and known camera intrinsics; no nav-graph data)

numbers_note: The paper states the 500-episode RxR-CE subset for the zero-shot evaluation. It does not say whether the distilled supervised RxR-CE result uses the full val-unseen set; it is marked 'full' here by assumption. Zero-shot RxR-CE numbers (500-episode subset) are compared in the paper against baselines (e.g. A2Nav) whose evaluation set is not stated, so the comparison may not be strictly like-for-like. Additional numbers not listed as entries: waypoint-predictor Chamfer distance 1.08 (vs 1.04 for ETPNav's MP3D-trained predictor); Grounded SAM floor segmentation 71.3% mIoU on ~1000 Habitat images. Further ablations on the 100-episode subset: w/o Instructions 36/24/14.6, w/o Waypoint Definitions 35/23/14.7, w/o Affordances 27/15/7.2 (OSR/SR/SPL); Zero-Shot Predictor + Baseline Agent 31/20/12.4; Supervised Predictor + Baseline Agent 34/23/13.1; GPT-4o low + Gemini high 23/11/6.9; Gemini both 25/14/9.1.
results: Zero-shot AO-Planner reaches 25.5 SR / 16.6 SPL on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split and 22.4 SR / 15.1 SPL on a 500-episode RxR-CE val-unseen subset. This beats the previous best zero-shot method A2Nav (22.6/11.1 and 16.8/6.3), which needs simulator data to train low-level policies. The distilled variant (ETPNav predictor trained on LLM pseudo-labels instead of MP3D nav-graph ground truth, plus the ETPNav agent) reaches 47 SR / 33 SPL on R2R-CE and 43.3 SR / 30.5 SPL on RxR-CE. That beats NaVid and DC-VLN but trails ETPNav (57/49).
limitations: Large gap to supervised methods remains: 25.5 zero-shot SR vs 57 for ETPNav, and the distilled variant also trails ETPNav. The authors attribute this partly to low-quality Habitat reconstructions and to LLM unfamiliarity with VLN-CE.
Costly and slow API-driven pipeline. RxR-CE is evaluated on only 500 episodes and ablations on 100 episodes; fine-tuning an agent with the LLM predictor in the loop would need ~9.6M calls (~20K USD).

Failure modes: Grounded SAM sometimes segments walls or tables as ground, and waypoints that are too far cause collisions (~30% of failures). High-level PathAgent direction and stop errors dominate (~70%). Performance is also highly sensitive to the choice of LLM per stage.
